 LeBron James has made himself a target of scrutiny in recent months. The 76ers star's partnership with Polymarket , the prediction market that allows users to sports bet as well as place wagers on mass casualty events like wars and natural disasters, made him the target of scorn among masses of basketball enjoyers ahead of the start of the regular season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Three weeks into the campaign, James once again has returned to the spotlight for his relationship to the gambling industry. These ties are far more nebulous in nature, with a nascent sports betting company appearing to opt to use James' name and likeness to promote its interests — all without being granted permission from James and his legal team.
 Suffice to say, James doesn't appear to be too pleased. Here's what you need to know about James' feud with Bron, the sports betting company that brandished an AI version of James to garner interest in its services.
 MORE: Steve Kerr trolls Donald Trump with $5,000 check jab after elections result 
 LeBron James cease and desist letter
 James sent a cease and desist letter to Bron, marketed as the "TikTok" for sports betting, a spokesperson for James told Front Office Sports on Thursday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "LeBron is in no way affiliated with this unauthorized use of his likeness," the spokesperson said.
 In the letter, James states Bron's unauthorized us of James' likeness is "especially serious and egregious" due to James' exclusive endorsement deal with Polymarket. The promotional trailer also suggests that James bets on basketball, a violation of league rules.
 The letter, sent by law firm Grubman Shire Meiselas & Sacks PC, called on Bron to immediately stop using James' likeness. James' lawyers also demanded that the company notify every person who used the app, in writing, that James has no involvement with the company.
 A copy of the cease and desist letter can be found here .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Not even Shaq and Charles Barkley can believe what Victor Wembanyama just did 
 What is 'Bron' sports betting company?
 Founded by Anish Gupta and Marc Zoghby in 2025, Bron labels itself as the TikTok for sports betting. The platform sees users be able to scroll through curated bets catered by an algorithm. Users can select wagers that intrigue them and use the platform to place bets to the sportsbook or prediction market of their choice.
 Bron dropped its teaser trailer on Wednesday. The 90-second-long creation was decked with AI-generated images, one of which included saw James scrolling through his phone to look for players to bet on.
 The name of the entity — and its link to James — was emphasized in the video, with AI-generated spectators querying where "Bron" was in the lead-up to a game. The prospect of linking James to betting on games — a violation of NBA rules — likely drew alarm bells from James' legal team.
